Why edited at all: a false claim of enforcement is worse than none, because it stops the next reader from checking -- the tree's own rule. title: Fan-out off `total` — R7 executed in the season loop (19_PLAN.md step 1 / 21_RECONCILIATION.md PHASE 1 step 2)
summary: THE DEFAULT `fan_out_mode` MOVES `total` -> `all_five` IN `engine/season/data/fixtures.py`. `total` fans every Event to every person, which is R7's ECHO MODEL arriving at the deposit layer: nothing is hideable, so there is no secret, no lie, no rumour, and no such thing as being absent. R7 ruled the architecture model — legitimacy falls where the news has reached. `total` stays as H-33's control arm and #353 S61's specified behaviour; the channel list is untouched (19_PLAN.md step 1: do not touch the arm set). H-33 STAYS `assumption`: R7 rules which arm DOES NOT ship -- between `presence_only` and `all_five` the ruling is SILENT and that choice was made on measurement, not by ruling -- and it says nothing about what the five predicates are. ⚠ The grade's WEIGHT changed even though the grade did not: under `total` the predicates were never consulted; under `all_five` they decide every deposit. MEASURED, build_world(0), 3 seasons: deposits 649 -> 60; ledgers [200,200,200] -> [0,28,32]; questions raised 5/9/10 -> 5/9/10 at `all_five` and 5/8/8 at `presence_only`, which is why the arm is `all_five`. CONTROL, AND IT IS WEAKER THAN THE FIRST WRITING OF THIS ENTRY CLAIMED: 122 probes re-run, ZERO verdict changes (63 PASS / 59 GAP either side), and their measured DETAILS moved substantially (A28's event count 7,836 -> 127, W6's plague reaching 35 ledgers -> 9, A5's log content hash). But probe and case verdicts resolve partly against register `grade:` cells rather than run behaviour (`harness/exercises.py:275-280`: `absent` blocks, `assumption` passes as assumed, `ruled`/`measured` pass), and two probes pin `fan_out_mode` themselves. So this is a MODERATE control -- the probes executed and nothing flipped -- not the strong one labelling it `CONTROL:` implied. Found by the adversarial pass. ARTIFACT: two persons' witness-deposit sets are IDENTICAL under `total` (0 differing pairs) and differ under the shipped arm — the first secret in the world, pinned with the `total` control inside the same test. ⚠ M-6 CANNOT FAIL AS SPECIFIED and is not reported as passed: `_r3_propagates` walks Event.causes[] over driver.resolved and never reads a ledger, so the corpus tallies (NPC R3 30/30, ARC 54/59) are identical across all three arms both co-located AND dispersed to distinct rungs. What is claimed is narrower: links 1 and 2 of the claim->question->act chain survive the flip. ⛔ THE COST IS LARGER THAN THE FIRST WRITING OF THIS ENTRY SAID, AND THE ARGUMENT THAT DISCOUNTED IT IS REFUTED. That writing called it a 16-fork artifact and cited H-54's hash-ordering share (801 of 1,068) as why 16 forks cannot rank the arms. TWO ERRORS, both found by an adversarial pass. (a) 801/1,068 was measured at fan_out_mode=total and cited to justify leaving total — wd_acceptance.fixtures_for never sweeps fan_out_mode. Re-run at all_five: 801 of 1,068, IDENTICAL in all six cells, with 39 of 108 fields moved so the re-run was no no-op. The number survives; citing it unrun did not. (b) The corpus-scale control existed, chunked and ready, and was not run. Run now — 89 worlds, 1,467 genuine forks, narrow cell, at observation_deposit_mode `actor`: total 62 of 1467 (95.77% reconvergence) · all_five 0 of 1467 (100.00%) · presence_only 229 of 1467 (84.39%). ZERO OF 1,467 IS NOT A SLICE ARTIFACT. At the SHIPPED arm a fork never changes a later decision, and presence_only — rejected here on a 2-question difference in one 3-person world — is nearly 4x the pre-flip arm. ⭐⭐ AND THE ZERO IS NOW DIAGNOSED, WHICH RETIRES THE ARM QUESTION RATHER THAN ANSWERING IT. A fork reaches a later decision by exactly ONE route: §F1 clause 4 (shape.py:627, belief_contradicts). Counting that population over the same 89 worlds (wd_extra.corpus_drops) at observation_deposit_mode `actor`: total 37 drops / 62 divergences · all_five 0 / 0 · presence_only 114 / 229. THE DIVERGENCES TRACK THE DROPS EXACTLY, so the zero is neither a property of the arm nor a channel defect — clause 4 never fires at the shipped configuration and a fork has nothing to change. Beliefs still form there (22 false-when-recorded) and contradict nothing. ⭐ EVERY CLAUSE-4 DROP IN THE WHOLE CORPUS, IN EVERY CELL, IS THE VERB `move` REFUSING ON A `contain.path:<person>` BELIEF — *there is no road from here to there*, formed by witnessing travel.blocked and overturned by a later travel.moved. Nothing else fires clause 4 at all. So the metric measures PEOPLE BEING WRONG, and a wider channel set does not suppress propagation: it CORRECTS THE STALE BELIEF BEFORE IT CAN BITE. ⚠ THE ARM IS THEREFORE NOT CHOSEN ON IT IN EITHER DIRECTION — a monoculture of one verb and one predicate, and tuning the knowledge layer to preserve `move`'s refusals would protect a single worked instance. THE DEFECT EXPOSED IS THAT §F1 CLAUSE 4 HAS EXACTLY ONE REACHABLE INSTANCE IN THE CORPUS, a producer hole and the place the work goes. The shipped arm stays 19_PLAN.md step 1's, which is also the only arm producing a secret between two co-located people. NON-MONOTONIC in the channel set, since all_five is a superset of presence_only. Half the channel survives: under the widened (verb, subject) fingerprint `actor` still diverges 8 against the control's 6 (was 11 against 7), so W-B still changes what a person deliberates ABOUT and no longer changes the verb set. The arm is NOT re-chosen on it, per CLAUDE.md §0 tests 3 and 5: 19_PLAN.md step 1 names the channel-predicate arm, and H-54 registers that within-source question order is decided by lexicographic order over content hashes in 801 of 1,068 deliberations, so a 16-fork slice supports no ranking of the arms. ⚠ AND ONE REGISTERED ARGUMENT EXPIRED: the ledger cap now evicts NOTHING in any arm (48/49/204 -> 0/0/0), so H-122's first reason for defaulting to `actor` — that `total` flattens H-40 — is gone. ⛔ AND ITS SECOND REASON IS ALSO GONE, which a first writing of this entry got wrong: form 6 IS `claim.held`, and `LEDGER_DERIVED_STEMS` excludes that stem at the deposit site UNCONDITIONALLY (`shape.py:3789`), so `total` cannot put a holder-relative value in any ledger. That leg died 2026-09-04 with the W-B exclusion, BEFORE R7. So `actor`-over-`total` rests on NEITHER stated reason; the default is still not moved, because that would be a second design change riding a measurement in flux. Recorded on the row.

description: THE WRIT AND THE WORD -- document 02 of proposals/2026-09-17-governance-and-holdings-r2/, the round-two centrepiece. PROPOSED, HELD BACK IN FULL. It answers the question ARCH F.15 files as an OPEN GAP: how does authority descend without broadcast? Round one missed that holonic_ARCHITECTURE.md S37.1 ALREADY SPECIFIES the mechanism, by reading S37.3's four prohibitions without the specification above them. Verbatim from S37.1: *'It travels by being noticed, NOT DOWN A CHAIN OF POSTS'*; *'A published dispensation does not apply -- it lands as a compliance contest, per relevant Rung, through `contest`, and SCOPE ENUMERATES EXECUTORS, NOT PLACES'*; *'Delivery is not assumed, and an executor who never received it is DISTINCT from one who received it and refused.'* THE MODEL, shaped by four Jordan rulings of 2026-09-17: TWO PEOPLE-BORNE CHANNELS and MATTER READS NO POLICY AT ALL. The WRIT is a Record of kind `dispensation` minted by `issue`, carried by a person's own `move`, handed over by `give`, arriving VERBATIM OR NOT AT ALL -- its only variance is forgery, copies and destruction. The WORD is `tell`, lossy ONLY at `Partial` on the receiver's Claim, and only by omission or operand drift within a stated band. Jordan's corrections, each of which removed a knob rather than adding one: *'what reaches a hamlet better correspond to some degree what the Duke wrote down… the game can't function as a game where the player can feel their choices mattering if all dissemination of information is so noisy that it's moot'*; *'A document from the Duke isn't like a game of telephone -- the written letter in some form with fidelity would end up being directly given to the settlement leader'*; and *'speed of a writ can be the same as word of it given that the message can be delivered directly as required to those who must implement it'* -- so SPEED IS NOT A DISTINGUISHING AXIS and the two are INDEPENDENT ARRIVALS whose ordering is itself a situation. What a writ buys is fidelity, addressing and EVIDENCE: a physical object that can be produced, checked, forged or destroyed, which is what makes the man holding it the authority on what it says to everyone who cannot read it -- and checkable, at a cost, by someone who travels. ONE DEPOSIT RULE covers commissions, works and petitions alike. NEEDS JORDAN -- RR-P, a CANDIDATE AXIOM. Jordan, verbatim: *'the player must have the sanctity of their choices/actions/decisions preserved in terms of the contents of those choices/actions/decisions themselves -- the worldly churn is in how those contents are received and acted upon by others.'* Stated as THE ACT IS INVIOLATE; THE RECEPTION IS NOT, with the test A DRAW MAY DECIDE WHAT HAPPENS; IT MAY NEVER DECIDE WHAT YOU MEANT, three boundaries (narrowing an option set is legitimate; failure is not corruption; intent reassignment is the forbidden shape), and its existing home in the Act/Claim split. Adoption as AX-7 would bind EVERY subsystem, not only governance, which is why it is escalated rather than assumed. GRADE: paper.

description:
THE CHARACTER MODEL AND THE DECISION LAYER, RULED BY JORDAN ACROSS ONE SESSION. One ruling event, one subject, one id by lane precedent (ED-IN-0233 covers two documents under one id; ED-IN-0244/0245 covered nine rulings across two). NOTHING IS IMPLEMENTED HERE: this records the rulings and lands the authoring surface they need. The rename, the cells and the verbs are R6-atomic and wait on the cells. 

THE BASIS. `Person.convictions` -> `Person.pursuits`; `conviction_axes` -> `pursuit_axes`. The rows are PURSUITS -- something a person is AFTER, not a position they hold -- which is why Authority, Precedent, Utility, Equity and Identity did not survive: they were institutional positions. FIFTEEN: virtue, honour, liberty, justice, wealth, reputation, scholastics, stability, individuality, community, faith, happiness, family, love, warden. SEVEN BIPOLAR AXES, both poles named: hierarchical/equal, precedent/substantive, partisan/equitable, selfish/selfless, rigid/flexible, grandiose/humble, deontological/instrumental. 

THREE NAMES WERE CHANGED AGAINST MEASURED COLLISIONS, counted on .py/.yaml over engine/season + systems + references, non-test. `status` (510 hits, the ubiquitous field key) -> `reputation`, which is CLEAN: all 25 hits are prose, and `options.py:477`'s `standing_of` docstring already uses 'reputation' as the CONTRASTING concept. `standing` was considered and REFUSED at 404 hits for a better reason than the count -- `standing_of` computes a GAP where low is good, so a pursuit of standing inverts polarity against it. `order` (442 hits: canonical order, act order, sort order) -> `authority` -> `stability`; `authority` was refused because #358 rev.2 s.E.2.2 rules AUTHORITY IS A PROPERTY OF THE SEAT BEING EXERCISED, NEVER OF THE PERSON EXERCISING IT, and a pursuit is by definition a property of the person. `stability` also fixes an independence problem `authority` had: you can want a stable EQUAL society, so it is orthogonal to hierarchical/equal in a way a pursuit of command would not be. `partial` -> `partisan`; `partial` collides with the requirements register's own state value (126 hits). ⚠ THE NAMING METHOD WAS PARTLY WRONG AND IS CORRECTED HERE: `names_index.yaml:127-128` already namespaces a busy word (`mech.stability` vs `fac.stability` vs `clock.ms`), so hunting for unused words was the wrong test for DATA. It remains the right test for PROSE and for polarity, which namespacing cannot fix -- and `Person.stance`, which has FOUR live senses and no names_index entry at all, is what happens without it. 

DROPPED. `Person.marks` -- a write-matrix row retired by W2 whose FIELD outlived it; zero readers, zero writers, no canon referent. `Person.orient` -- never built, and now redundant: self/other lives in the pursuit space (wealth, reputation, individuality against community, family, love), so a field would be a second home for one fact. `benefits_me` and the 38-row beneficiary column SURVIVE -- the selfish axis score supplies the disposition, the column the per-candidate fact. THAT DISSOLVES R7's OBJECTION rather than hitting it: R7 says a projected axis cannot vary at fixed weights, and it no longer needs to, because two people with identical pursuits ARE identically disposed and the variation comes from the candidates. `sacred` leaves the moral basis for `Person.conviction`, carrying religious affiliation intensity (R1/R2, ED-IN-0251) -- it was always a religious word in a moral basis. 

KILL / WOUND IS NOT A VERB, and the finding behind the ruling is larger than the ruling. MEASURED: only 2 of 38 verbs carry `contests` at all -- `kill / wound` -> the body, `tell` -> a standing -- and the personal-combat engine is registered `@provider('contest','personal_combat')`. So `kill / wound` is the ONLY route to it, and it is excluded from `resolvable_verbs` because its `requires` is `—` (driver.py:139 keeps Jordan's 2026-09-02 *you can't just kill or wound* true). CONSEQUENCE: THE PERSONAL-COMBAT SEAM HAS NO PERSON-SIDE DOOR -- nobody in a season can start a fight, because the only door to the fight is labelled with its result. The row was carrying the ATTEMPT's job because no attempt verb existed. RULED: `fight` (opponent is `subject`, needs a typed precondition or it fails driver.py:146 exactly as kill/wound does), and the duel pair `challenge` -> `accept`, with `accept` carrying `contests: "the body"`. `duel` is not a verb either: it is the name of what resolves. The seam wrapper is already verb-agnostic (it takes a prize and claimants and 'decides nothing itself'), so legibility was never the issue. `H-80`, filed to ADMIT kill/wound to resolvable_verbs, is refused by this ruling. 

DEONTOLOGY IS A REFUSAL AND IT GATES. Jordan: *it's a refusal to take certain actions. It gates actions insofar as the weighting is a threshold for certain actions.* So the weight IS the threshold and there is one mechanism, not two: a candidate whose `align(verb, deontological)` sits beyond what the person tolerates NEVER FORMS. Site is `opening_set(p, v, q, fx)` -- person-side, no World, AX-2 intact. `score` cannot express refusal: it ranks, and at tau=0.1 a good enough outcome outranks any finite penalty, so a deontologist as a score term is an instrumentalist with a strong preference. Jordan's own definitions, recorded because a prior session conflated them: deontological/instrumental is WHAT MAKES AN ACT PERMISSIBLE, precedent/substantive is WHERE YOU LOOK FOR THE ANSWER. Orthogonal -- all four corners are populated -- so a high measured `r` between them is a PLACEMENT defect, not a redundant axis. 

SCARS: THE DIAGNOSIS AND THE LAWFUL WRITE. The design (`conviction_track_v1.md` s2, quarantined, reference for intent) has scars accrue from WITNESSING morally-loading events, counted PER ELEMENT, with thresholds at 1 (destabilise), 2 (WEIGHT SHIFTS, others gain proportionally) and 3+ (crisis; terminal -- restabilise, fold, or be destroyed). THAT IS THE ONLY THING IN THE DESIGN THAT CLOSES THE DECISION LOOP, and the loop is measurably open: 2,403 forks reconverge 100%, later-decision divergence ~4%. WHAT WAS BUILT SUBSTITUTED ALL THREE LEGS -- trigger witnessing -> being wounded (item 21's L4 amendment), key per-element -> per-AXIS (`_scar` reads ALIGNMENT), and type COUNT -> continuous float (`scar_step x cell`). The third is why `scar_step` parked at 0 with no reader: it is a magnitude for a mechanic whose unit is 'how many times'. RULED: scars apply to BOTH tracks (pursuits AND convictions), the unit is a COUNT, thresholds 1/2/3. 

AND THE RESOLVE-vs-WITNESS QUESTION IS SETTLED RATHER THAN DEFERRED. L4 (holonic_ARCHITECTURE.md:173) constrains WHO writes, not WHEN: *`social: true` means ONLY AN ACT MAY WRITE IT*. At WITNESS the writer is the world processing an Event -- the violation item 21 names. At RESOLVE the writer is the ACT, which is lawful. And 'who witnessed' is NOT private to WITNESS: `epistemic.py:440 observers_for(w, e, mode, everyone)` is a STANDALONE function that WITNESS calls, so RESOLVE can call it too and there is one owner of perception (s8) rather than a duplicated predicate. Witnessing is already selective -- MEASURED: `fan_out_mode = all_five` is the shipped ruled default (2026-09-07, R7) over chronicle/co_located/document_key/post_remit/witness_key. SO THE LAWFUL FORM IS: at RESOLVE, after the act's Event is formed, the act calls `observers_for` and writes a scar on each observer whose pursuits or convictions that act violated. Item 21 was right that WITNESS cannot write it and wrong to conclude the scar must fall back to 'the outcome that names the person' -- that threw away the crowd to solve a problem the crowd was not causing. ⚠ DECLARED DIVERGENCE: `observers_for` at RESOLVE and at WITNESS can differ on `co_located`, because WITNESS is the join and a later act can move someone; the scar then reflects who was present WHEN IT HAPPENED, which is the more correct reading for witnessing but is a real difference between two calls to one function. 

ONE RECORD CORRECTED IN PASSING. `witness.py:94-95` asserted the channel predicates do not exist and the fan-out is therefore total -- false, and contradicted SIX LINES BELOW IT by `W6`/`H-33`'s own note. A reader taking it at its word concludes witnessing is unselective, which is how the scar mechanic came to be written against participants instead of observers. Same class as the six records ED-IN-0260 corrected. 

WHAT THIS COMMIT LANDS: the worksheet (`proposals/2026-09-20-pursuit-basis-worksheet.yaml`, 15x7 = 105 cells, alignment re-cell over 40 verbs, the scar model, and what is open), a supersession banner on the 2026-09-18 worksheet (kept because ED-IN-0251 R3 cites it and its religious cells carry forward), and the witness.py correction. WHAT IT DOES NOT LAND: the rename (483 occurrences in engine/season non-test, 392 in references owners; `registers/`'s 403 must NOT be rewritten, they are the record of what was said when), the 105 cells, the verbs, and the scar rebuild -- all R6-atomic and all downstream of the cells, which are Jordan's under STR-6/R3. MEASURED-BY: engine/season/harness/conviction_spread.py -- the instrument that scores any placement, reporting magnitude, within_60deg, pairwise r and participation ratio. 

AMENDED SAME DAY: `faith` KEEPS ITS ROW, ruled. `Person.conviction` is which side you are on and how intensely; the `faith` PURSUIT is how much of yourself goes into religious matters at all. Orthogonal -- intensely orthodox and never acting on it, or lukewarm with a life organised around church politics, are both expressible. Jordan verbatim: *"someone who is a devout church of Solmund follower want to do work for the church or someone who is pure Einhir and anti Solmund church whose faith work is about dismantling it."* ⚠ AND THE PAIR IS RECORDED AS THE PLACEMENT'S FALSIFIER RATHER THAN AN ILLUSTRATION: both score HIGH on `faith` and want opposite things, so only the AXES can separate them. That is precisely the discrimination ED-IN-0214 measured the old basis failing -- nine of thirteen rows within 60 degrees of one mean vector, so two people sharing a primary came out the same. After the 105 cells are placed, score the two; if they do not land far apart the placement is wrong, and `conviction_spread`'s `within_60deg` is the aggregate form of the same check. 

SECOND AMENDMENT SAME DAY, AND IT REVERSES THIS ROW'S OWN RULING. Jordan, after the row was committed: *"admit kill and wound as resolvable verbs."* WHAT THIS ROW SAID: *`H-80`, filed to ADMIT kill/wound to resolvable_verbs, is refused by this ruling.* THAT REFUSAL IS WITHDRAWN. What survives unamended is the rest of the verb ruling -- `fight`, and the duel pair `challenge` -> `accept` -- which was never in conflict with it: those are the acts a person DECLARES, and the admission is about whether the fold can carry a body-contest at all. The two answers are independent and both are now yes. 

WHAT WAS BUILT, AND IT RUNS (CLAUDE.md s0.2). `kill / wound` is in `resolvable_verbs()` -- 18 verbs -> 19 -- and EXECUTES IN 47 OF THE 89 LIVE CORPUS WORLDS. Until this commit `@provider('contest','personal_combat')` was registered and unreachable from a season: the personal-combat engine had NO PERSON-SIDE DOOR, which is the finding this row already carried. THE ADMISSION ITSELF IS ONE CELL -- a typed `requires` on the row (`existence` of `subject`, kind `Person`) -- because `driver.py`'s contest gate excludes a contested verb that is UNTYPED, on the ground that `operands_for` returns `{}` for one and the seam would get a single claimant. Typing the row binds `subject`, which IS the second claimant, so the gate's own recorded reason stopped holding. The clause is the narrowest that does the job and is not a stand-in: you cannot fight someone who is not there, and `Person.exists` is the field the `Felled` band writes. 

THREE FOLD DEFECTS HAD TO BE FIXED BEFORE IT RAN, EACH MEASURED, EACH AT ONE OWNER, AND ALL THREE WERE LATENT RATHER THAN NEW -- invisible for as long as no contested verb could be chosen. (1) `resolve()`'s CONTEST BRANCH SKIPPED ELIGIBILITY AND `requires` ENTIRELY. sE2's order is *eligibility -> requires -> resolve* and the branch is the alternative to `_fold`, which is where both checks lived, so a contested act was carried into personal combat without its precondition ever being read. MEASURED on admission: 85 of 143 corpus cases became whole-case DESIGN-GAPs, 74 of them PARTY-GAP -- *claimant not a person: 'p_a' / 'rec:cb377aad7694a2da'* -- because `opening_set` binds `subject` from the question's referent and a referent is usually a Record or a Rung. FIXED by extracting `_admits(w, a, row)` and calling it from BOTH paths (s8: one owner); a refused contested act emits `emits_on_refusal` and is witnessed rather than raising. (2) EVERY PERSON WAS OFFERED THEMSELVES AS AN ADVERSARY. `opening_set` offers every person themselves as a referent for every verb -- 49.6% of all candidates name the actor as their own subject -- so the commonest contested candidate in the corpus was a man attacking himself, and 47 more cases died on *personal combat needs two parties; got 1*. FIXED person-side, off the ROW'S OWN `contests:` column and never a verb name: a contest needs two claimants and a person is not their own adversary, which is `move`'s *a node is not a path to itself* one seam over. (3) A DEAD PERSON WENT ON ACTING, AND ALSO WENT ON BEING CONFERRED OFFICES. s27.1 says each act sees the world its predecessors left, and until a man could be killed inside the fold nothing tested what his successor does. Two faults, one root -- THE DEAD STAYED REFERENCEABLE: `World.remove_person` popped `persons` and left the person's own `person`-kind RUNG standing, which is exactly the id-scheme ambiguity `class_of`'s docstring warns about (persons is scanned first, so the id reads Person while they live and silently becomes Rung the moment they do not), and 11 cases died on `_refuse_bad_hold` -- *`hold` tenure has subject 'p_c', which is a Rung* -- because `confer` seated an office on a corpse; and 2 more (`ARC-10`, `ARC-12`) reached the seam with a dead FIRST claimant. FIXED at the two owners: the node dies with the person in `remove_person` (kind checked, not assumed), and the fold emits `act.ineligible` for an actor a predecessor removed. 

THE CORPUS RETURNS TO ITS PRE-ADMISSION BAR ON EVERY COUNT BUT ONE, both arms at seed 0 over the same 143 cases, control from this tree with the five files stashed: DESIGN-GAP 0 -> 85 -> 0, R1 89/89 -> 4/89 -> 89/89, UNREPRESENTABLE 54 unmoved. THE ONE EXCEPTION IS REPORTED RATHER THAN SMOOTHED: `NPC-009` moves RUNS-UNDECLARED -> RUNS-ALONE-UNDECLARED, a death breaking that case's propagation, which is the mechanic working. SEVEN ARTIFACT NUMBERS MOVED AND EACH IS RE-PINNED WITH ITS CONTROL, NOT ADJUSTED: distinct executed sets 44 -> 57 (variety rose; the universal set `{create_record, utter}` was re-taken IN THE SAME BREATH and did NOT move, so this is not the `U1` shape); eight verbs reach fewer worlds for the scenes the contest takes, NAMED rather than netted off, AND SEPARATED FROM THE FOLD FIXES BY A THIRD ARM rather than attributed whole to the admission -- which is the correction a control bought and the two-arm reading had wrong. THREE ARMS, same 89 live worlds, seed 0: BASELINE (nothing) -> FOLD FIXES ONLY (the admission monkey-patched off at the loaded row, so `resolvable_verbs()` is 18 again) -> BOTH. The fold fixes ALONE move four verbs and move variety NOT AT ALL -- distinct sets 44 -> 44 -- `tell` 72 -> 70 (its precondition is now read BEFORE the seam, which is defect 1 biting the other contested row), `interview` 53 -> 57, `release` 10 -> 12, `research` 63 -> 64. THE ADMISSION IS WHAT MOVES THE REST, on top of that arm: distinct 44 -> 57, `interview` 57 -> 46, `tell` 70 -> 63, `speak` 82 -> 78, `move` 51 -> 47, `surveil` 58 -> 55, `transfer` 77 -> 75, `release` 12 -> 9, `research` 64 -> 63. That variety is the admission's and none of it is the refactor's; clause-4 drops 8 -> 9; `W-D` fork divergence at the `total` arm 7 -> 8 with the denominator unmoved at 31 -- MORE divergence, which is the direction R-01/R-02 want; maturation depth ceiling `depths[6]` 12 -> 11 (act-mix-driven by that test's own argument, and `depths[3]` unmoved is the control). TWO COMMITTED ARTIFACTS RE-RECORDED DELIBERATELY (`CASELOG_NPC.md`, `results.json`) and the re-record is the PAYOFF rather than bookkeeping: case rows reading *'kill / wound' is on the table and the fold cannot execute it* now read PASS, and `NPC-010`'s core_blocked falls 2 -> 1. CONTROLS THAT DID NOT MOVE, stated because an absence is the cheapest claim to make: the headless content hash is `80789994e376c5304c5f8acce4a3b4d7` before and after, `m1_acceptance` holds `ab77c30d273b` with 0 stub invocations, and 24 headless seeds x 4 seasons + 2 populated report 0 invariant violations over 16,194 events. 

WHAT IS STILL OPEN AND IS NOT THIS AMENDMENT'S. THE SLASHED NAME SURVIVES and is separately ruled wrong (*"kill / wound isn't supposed to be a verb by itself"*). Splitting it into `kill` and `wound` needs a row of ALIGNMENT cells each, and `ALIGNMENT` is being re-celled whole over the seven `pursuit_axes` -- so the split rides that commit, where the cells are authored once, rather than inventing two rows of four old-basis cells that are about to be deleted. `fight` and `challenge` -> `accept` ride the same commit for the same reason.

source: Jordan's instruction in this session, 2026-10-28
description: RULED BY JORDAN 2026-10-28, in session, answering the question ED-IN-0302 left open (whether 'container' should become 'scene'). His words, verbatim: "Match Godot terminology in all instances." DECISIONS: Godot's words name Godot constructs. A registered module's playable form is a SCENE (a PackedScene, .tscn); a scene that runs is a SCENE INSTANCE, and the act budget counts them; the sim's record of one stays `Scene`. 'Scene' is used as Godot uses it (the saved definition and, loosely, the running thing, with 'instance' as the descriptor when the difference matters), so the sim's Scene record and the roughly one thousand prose uses of 'scene' for an occasion are already Godot-idiomatic and are NOT renamed. 'Container' is retired from this repo's own vocabulary for that sense; it survives only in quotations, field names, plan titles, ED names, file names and non-game senses (a dev container, a data structure). Where a Godot construct had another name here (the 'Godot shell', 'presentation shell') it is the scene tree, in game/. KEPT, because Godot has no word for them: rung, holon, carrier (a design category, implemented as script classes), module (one ordinary word with host and registered descriptors), manifest, composition row, seam, host. NEVER reused as a class name: Container, Node, Path, Resource, Environment. system: infrastructure/cross-cutting (IN; a heard claim goes stale, the opinion it formed does not, and hearing it again makes it more likely to be believed; workplan v11 CR-82)
citations: engine/season/hole_register.yaml -- H-40 (no reader separates one confidence from another)
source: Jordan, 2026-11-04, two messages in one sitting, a second ruling and its addendum on CR-82 (after ED-IN-0319); written by a session of B10-09 close two.
description: JORDAN'S RULING, 2026-11-04, extending ED-IN-0319. His words, verbatim: "the thing with claims is about whether they are still relevant: if you hear someone performed an action or a faction accomplished something, it is possible for your information to become stale over time as you may not hear about any updated circumstances. if something is stale for a long length of time, you may be aware that your information is outdated. what remains the case though is your opinion about what that person has done". RULED: a claim about what someone did or what a faction accomplished is information that can go STALE (nothing updates it) and, once stale for long, the holder can KNOW it is stale; but the OPINION the holder formed of the person or faction from it REMAINS. WHAT THE CODE HAS (read 2026-11-04): claim confidence decays each season (`claim_decay_per_season`, `loop/matter.py`) and the eviction ranks confidence x (when + 1), lowest first, so a stale claim is evicted first (`state/ledgers.py`); `Person.stance` rows `(referent, valence, weight)` are a stored opinion that `queries/person_q.py::stance_toward` reads, written only by combat effects (`loop/effects_combat.py`) today; `deeds_judged` re-derives what a person makes of a referent's deeds from the CLAIMS he holds, so the judgment vanishes when the claim is evicted; `hole_register.yaml` H-40 found no reader separates one confidence from another, so no reader knows a claim is stale. ADDENDUM, his next message, verbatim: "further if you repeatedly hear a similar claim or proposition about someone or something, you are more likely to believe it still the case going forward". RULED: corroboration. A claim heard again, similar to one already held, raises the holder's belief that it still holds and keeps it from going stale. WHAT THE CODE DOES (read 2026-11-04): none; `loop/witness.py` de-duplicates a repeat (`seen_obs`, and the direct-copy guard) so that it costs no `ledger_cap` slot, which is a capacity argument, and a repeat adds nothing to the holder's confidence or recency. The mechanism is NOT ruled. Built in CR-82's commit 2 (a re-hearing refreshes the held claim's recency and raises its confidence, bounded, in place of the suppression; the cap lever and the refresh are one design question: what a repeat does to a held claim) and read in commit 4. Built under workplan v11 CR-82 as its commits 3 and 4 (the opinion outlives the claim; what reads staleness), after the retention lever. [ASSUMPTION; medium; Jordan to correct; revert: drop commits 3 and 4]. This row records the ruling; the prose of CR-82 is reference (CLAUDE.md 0.05).

description: JORDAN'S RULING, 2026-11-04, extending ED-IN-0320. His words, verbatim: "if you hear something once and never again, you have less certainty" and "if you hear something with competing information, then you have to work off of your trust or deduce information by judgment". RULED: (1) a claim heard once and never again is held with less certainty than one heard again; (2) where claims compete, the holder settles them by how far he trusts the tellers, or deduces by judgment. WHAT THE CODE HAS (read 2026-11-04): `queries/person_q.py::LedgerReader` already ranks competing claims on one (subject, predicate) by `(support, when, confidence)` under a `weigh`, where `support` is the noisy-OR over the DISTINCT ORIGINS asserting the same value and `weigh` is the holder's trust in the teller (`decision/options.py::teller_weight`: told_weight ** hops x relation x record); a firsthand claim weighs 1.0, a claim heard once through a teller weighs less, and several distinct origins raise support; ONE ORIGIN REPEATING HIMSELF ADDS NOTHING (the reader's own rule), which ED-IN-0320's addendum does not say and Jordan has not ruled either way; every caller but `epistemic.belief_contradicts` passes `weigh=None`, so only that one reader grades by trust. WHAT IT LACKS: a reading of 'heard once and never again' as a lower certainty outside `belief_contradicts`, and any deduction by judgment where trust does not separate the claims. The mechanism is NOT ruled. Folded into workplan v11 CR-82's commit 4 (what reads certainty: the `weigh` callers, and where the design already names one, `said_of`'s, the weighing built; the same-origin repeat a decision recorded with its reasoning, not asked). system: infrastructure/cross-cutting (IN; belief in a heard claim rests on trust, on the count of distinct origins and on fit with what the holder knows; workplan v11 CR-82)
source: Jordan, 2026-11-04, restating the claim model after ED-IN-0322; written by a session of B10-09 close two.
description: JORDAN'S RULING, 2026-11-04. His words, verbatim: "yes. so if I only hear about something from one person, even if they repeat it a lot, i know that has less weight than if other people say that same thing too.....assuming that I don't have 100% trust in that one person of course. you're more liable to believe based upon trust AND count AND how well what is said matches your knowledge in context of that person or situation". RULED: how far a person believes a heard claim rests on three things together: (1) TRUST in the tellers, (2) the COUNT of distinct origins (one origin repeating adds nothing; at full trust one origin already suffices), and (3) FIT: how well what is said matches what he already knows of that person or situation. WHAT THE CODE HAS (read 2026-11-04): (1) and (2) are `queries/person_q.py::LedgerReader._support`, a noisy-OR over distinct origins weighted by `decision/options.py::teller_weight`; at a weight of 1.0 a single origin gives support 1.0, as ruled; only `epistemic.belief_contradicts` passes a `weigh`. (3) has NO term in `_support`: competing claims on one (subject, predicate) already compete by value, but nothing grades a claim by its fit with what the holder knows of the person (his `stance` rows, `person_q.deeds_judged`) or of the situation (his other held claims). The mechanism for (3) is NOT ruled and no carrier is to be coined for it: it is to be read from what the holder already holds. Folded into workplan v11 CR-82's commit 4 (what reads certainty), which builds a term only where the design already names a place and otherwise records the gap. RULED: stored CLOCKS AND COUNTERS belong to the game, among them a CHURCH INFLUENCE clock whose rise brings a theocratic attempted seizure after which the Church begins taking land; they are not coded yet. WHAT THE RECORD HAS (read 2026-11-05): the design vocabulary carries them as `category: clock` entries (`references/definitions/vocab_source.yaml:140-162`: Church Influence, CI, range 0-100, milestones at 40 Church Assertive, 55 Institutional Reach, 60 Mass Seizure available with a probabilistic declaration P = ((CI-60)/40)^3.3 per season, 65 Church Dominant, 80 Church Ascendant, 100 Theocracy Unification Attempt; renamed from Theocracy Counter per ED-782); `references/descriptor_registry.yaml:246` lists `clocks: [Evidence, CI, MS, IP]`; the archived (NOT CANON, intent and history only) `.designs/systems/overview/reference/clock_registry_v30.md` is the 'single source of truth for all clocks, tracks and counters' (Mending Stability 0-100 starting 60 and decaying; Church Influence 0-100 starting 28 rising; Institutional Pressure 0-100 starting 20 rising; Turmoil 0-10 rising; faction tracks such as loyalties, Popular Will, Warden Cooperation) and `peninsular_strain_v30.md` is the strain design. THE CODE HAS NONE: the endings roster says 'NOT CARRIED, BY THE CUTS: no stored stability or legitimacy value, no threshold counter, no clock (#457 section 5; T-a, T-b, T-c)' (`rosters.yaml:2928-2929`) and the strife master refuses 'No stored flow, state, phase or counter' and 'No self-worsening condition' (`00_MASTER.md:187-189`), and ED-IN-0301 confirmed 'M16's fourth motion (no)' and 'T-c (excluded)'. THIS ROW SUPERSEDES THOSE CUTS TO THE EXTENT THEY BAR A STORED GAME CLOCK OR COUNTER; the earlier rows are append-only and stay. WHICH CUTS SURVIVE (for example an actorless event written to standing or a seat, or a timer that advances with no actor feeding it) is NOT ruled here and is stated clause by clause in the unified design; scripting drift (CLAUDE.md section 0) is unaffected. The arc map's finding that a ratchet is 'barred by ratified rules' is therefore withdrawn as to stored clocks: it described the cuts, which Jordan has now lifted for the clocks of the game. The mechanism, the values and the clock list are NOT ruled and nothing is changed. This row records the ruling; the prose is reference (CLAUDE.md 0.05).

system: infrastructure/cross-cutting (IN; clocks and counters are not contradictory to emergence; refines ED-IN-0341 and ED-IN-0343)
source: Jordan, 2026-11-05, after ED-IN-0343; written by a session of B10-09 close two.
description: JORDAN'S RULING, 2026-11-05. His words, verbatim: "clocks/counters are not contradictory to emergence". RULED: a stored clock or counter, fed by the deeds of the world's actors, is compatible with emergence; the engine need not choose between them. This removes the reading under which a clock was a script. WHAT STANDS: the rule against scripting drift (CLAUDE.md section 0: no special-casing of an entity or outcome, no authored beat, no timer that advances with no actor feeding it) is not lifted; what Jordan lifts is the inference that a stored counter is itself scripted. No mechanism is ruled and nothing is changed. This row records the ruling; the prose is reference (CLAUDE.md 0.05).

system: infrastructure/cross-cutting (IN; what a clock is: it triggers behaviours from an accumulation of game-world events; refines ED-IN-0343 and ED-IN-0344)
source: Jordan, 2026-11-05, completing ED-IN-0344; written by a session of B10-09 close two.
description: JORDAN'S RULING, 2026-11-05. His words, verbatim: "they trigger behaviours based upon an accumulation of game world events". RULED: a clock or counter (ED-IN-0343, ED-IN-0344) is an ACCUMULATION OF GAME-WORLD EVENTS that TRIGGERS BEHAVIOURS when it reaches its thresholds. It is fed by events the world's actors produce and, once accumulated, brings about behaviour (the Church's theocratic seizure attempt and land-taking is the stated case). It is not a timer and not an authored beat: the thing that moves it is the events. WHAT THE CODE HAS: the event log (`w.log`) already records the world's events with causes, and `_standing_crossings` (`loop/matter.py`) reads a band crossing per person; no stored accumulation of events into a clock exists, and no threshold triggers a behaviour. HOW a clock reads events (which event kinds feed which clock, with what weight), what a threshold triggers (a verb becomes available or a person's choice is conditioned, rather than an act being imposed), and where it is stored are NOT ruled and nothing is changed. This row records the ruling; the prose is reference (CLAUDE.md 0.05).

system: infrastructure/cross-cutting (IN, SE, FA, WR: flow conditioning of decisions, office influence by institutional reach, the settlement fabric (Church-owned buildings, several cohorts), canon locations matched to the engine)
source: Jordan, in session, 2026-11-08: his statements T2, K1, K2, W1, T1, the influence and Church statements, the settlement and cohort descriptions, the permission to design from his rulings, the locations ruling, and his correction withdrawing the obstacle term (verbatim below).
description: RULINGS (Jordan, 2026-11-08, one session), recorded as a set for workplan v11's flow-conditioning, office-influence and settlement-fabric positions (CR-97 to CR-107 and the canon alignment, batches B11-F1 to B11-F3, part16). (1) T2: the system is layered, bottom-up granular and top-down holistic, joined by handshakes, so procedurally generated emergent narratives have legible plot points. (2) K1, K2 and W1: weighting decisions toward plausible outcomes is permitted, and characters unaware of a flow still have their actions modulated, under the split between what the character knows and chooses from and a world-side mechanism that conditions its field of decisions and choices. (3) The correction of 2026-11-08: no obstacle, target number, probability, pool or draw is touched; 'outcome' means how choices act on matters, events and characters through the existing resolvers, unmodified. (4) The field route (CR-100, CR-101) needs no Layer 1 hunk (World-first `questions_for`, `architecture/meta/04_CODE_ARCHITECTURE.md:168`; `decision/` untouched, `:171`); a weight inside `choose` (CR-105) breaches AX-2 as worded (`architecture/meta/01_AXIOMS.md:106`) and is built only under a hunk Jordan directs, in the style of H-L0-11, after CR-103's measurement. (5) The upward-influence rule: an office's influence follows the rung its institution covers, uniformly, never a named person; the Church is at the realm rung because it has churches and infrastructure of varying size in all territories. (6) T1 (the probabilistic-bias thesis) is kept as design intent, tested by CR-103, not ruled. (7) The settlement rules: buildings belong by default to the settlement and so to the governing faction; the Church of Solmund's buildings (places of worship, Templar quarters, schools and monasteries) are owned by the Church in every territory (CR-106); several cohorts per settlement along caste, creed and allegiance (CR-107); territory caps on developments and their sizes are out of scope (no position; the plan's Out of scope names the owner). (8) Canon territory locations are matched to engine reality: where canon prose and the engine place a settlement or territory differently, the engine wins and the prose is corrected (the canon alignment, part16 §3). VERBATIM (spelling as typed): T2: *"it is paramount that we have a layered system both bottom-up granular and top-down holistic with handshakes so that we can have procedurally generated emergent narratives that actually have legible plot points"*. K1: *"Determination of outcomes does not preclude incentivizing or weighting decisions/actions that could lead towards a set of plausible of outcomes based upon strife flows"*. K2: *"there should be a consequential ripple/cascade effect/propagation of worldly states and matters and issues and concerns based upon strife flows, which means that even characters who may be unaware of something are still likely to have their actions and outcomes modulated accordingly"*. W1: *"I am okay with breaking this axiom under the notion that there is a split between what the character of aware that they are choosing based on their knowledge and a mechanism whereby era regime and strife all condition the characters contextual field of decisions"*. T1: *"Without probabilistic bias, we will likely struggle to have enough events cohere at both depth and breadth to constitute a larger narrative or theme"*. Influence: *"impact upon era regime and strife by individual characters!! the big four of king Almud, Duke vaynare, Duchess baralta and church head himlensendt will have the greatest ability of characters to influence/impact/modify/direct era regime and strife that is because they have the most important offices so the amount of influence an office has, which has a relationship to the rung it is on, in turn determines the amount of impact on these high level narrative shapes of era regime strife"*. Church: *"Church is at kingdom rung for influence even though it only owns one territory because it has churches and infrastructure of varying size in all territories"*. Settlements: *"Settlements have cohorts (population groups), which represent the feelings and state of the settlement populace. There can be multiple cohorts (e.g. Northern Einhir & Southern Einhir) within a settlement who may have conflicting feelings/demands. Convergence and divergence for everyday needs are possible. Settlements have infrastructure. Infrastructure is represented through developments and buildings. Each settlement is within a territory that will dictate the caps upon how many developments/structures/buildings may be possible as well as their specific size. [...] All of these belong to the settlement and therefore the governing faction. The exception are the Church of Solmund buildings. There are places of worship of differing scale (chapels, churches and cathedrals), knights templar quarters of varying size, schools/monasteries. These are all owned by the Church of Solmund, never the faction owning the territory."* Cohort axes: *"Settlements require multiple different cohorts to represent the following dynamics: caste system, Einhir Revivalism vs Church of Solmund and/or Altonian Political System, faction allegiances"*. Permission: *"you have permission to design based upon my rulings and game context"*; *"I already gave you P11 information to build from"*. Locations: *"Canon territory locations should be matched to engine reality"*. The sign of an obstacle term: Jordan answered *"I don't know"* and then withdrew the term (the correction in the Status line). RATIFIED by Jordan's instruction of 2026-11-08 ("ratify all and merge"), including the items first held back: CR-105's AX-2 hunk as the wording to apply (not applied until CR-105's gate opens or he says so); the cohort and Church-site content as the accepted first reading (every row keeps its [ASSUMPTION] and revert); CR-107b (faction commitment) as a position behind its reader audit; the Schoenland engages cell at CR-107's build; territory caps as out of scope. CALLED OUT: the canon edits under item (8), live on merge.
